package com.example.model;

import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;

/**
 * Example Lombok entity: {@code @Data} generates getters, setters,
 * equals/hashCode and toString; the constructor annotations and
 * {@code @Builder} cover object creation.
 */
@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class User {
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
}
EOF
cat > src/test/java/com/example/model/UserTest.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.model;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class UserTest {

    @Test
    void lombokGeneratesAccessorsConstructorsAndBuilder() {
        User built = User.builder().id(1L).name("Ada").email("ada@example.com").build();
        User constructed = new User(1L, "Ada", "ada@example.com");

        User mutable = new User();
        mutable.setId(1L);
        mutable.setName("Ada");
        mutable.setEmail("ada@example.com");

        assertEquals("Ada", built.getName());
        assertEquals(built, constructed);
        assertEquals(built, mutable);
    }
}
EOF

I set up a Maven project in `/work` that uses **Lombok** to generate getters, setters and constructors. `mvn verify` passes, including a test that checks the generated code works.

**What's in it**
- **`pom.xml`**:
  - Lombok 1.18.48 with `provided` scope, so it's only used at compile time and isn't shipped with the app.
  - Lombok is also listed in the compiler plugin's `annotationProcessorPaths`. This is needed: on JDK 23 and later, the compiler no longer picks up Lombok from the classpath by itself, and without this line `@Data` and the other annotations would silently generate nothing.
  - Compiles for Java 25, with JUnit 6.1.3, compiler plugin 3.16.0 and surefire 3.6.0. I first wrote older versions, and the project's dependency-check hook told me to bump them to these.
- **`lombok.config`**: stops Lombok from reading config files in parent folders, and marks generated code so coverage tools like JaCoCo skip it.
- **`src/main/java/com/example/model/User.java`**: an example class using `@Data`, `@Builder`, `@NoArgsConstructor` and `@AllArgsConstructor`.
- **`src/test/java/.../UserTest.java`**: tests the builder, the constructors, the setters and getters, and `equals`.
- **`.gitignore`**: ignores `target/` and IDE files.

**Things to know**
- **Warning during the build:** on the installed JDK 26, Lombok prints a `sun.misc.Unsafe ... deprecated` warning. It doesn't break the build; it will go away once Lombok releases an update for newer JDKs.
- **IDE setup:** IntelliJ supports Lombok out of the box. VS Code and Eclipse need the Lombok plugin or extension, and each developer should turn on annotation processing.
- **For read-only data classes**, plain Java `record`s give you constructors, accessors, `equals` and `hashCode` without needing Lombok. Lombok is most useful for classes whose fields change, and for builders.

I haven't committed anything. You're on `master` and the main branch is `main`, so tell me which branch you want it on if you'd like a commit.

mkdir -p src/main/java/com/example/model src/test/java/com/example/model && cat > pom.xml <<'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>app</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.release>25</maven.compiler.release>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <lombok.version>1.18.48</lombok.version>
        <junit.version>5.13.4</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Compile-time only: generates getters/setters/constructors, not shipped at runtime -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
            <scope>provided</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.14.0</version>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- JDK 23+ no longer discovers annotation processors on the classpath
                         automatically, so Lombok must be registered explicitly. -->
                    <annotationProcessorPaths>
                        <path>
                            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
                            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
                            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
                        </path>
                    </annotationProcessorPaths>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.3</version>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>
EOF
cat > lombok.config <<'EOF'
# Stop Lombok config lookup from climbing into parent directories
config.stopBubbling = true
# Mark generated code so coverage tools (e.g. JaCoCo) skip it
lombok.addLombokGeneratedAnnotation = true
EOF
cat > src/main/java/com/example/model/User.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.model;

import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;

/**
 * Example Lombok entity: {@code @Data} generates getters, setters,
 * equals/hashCode and toString; the constructor annotations and
 * {@code @Builder} cover object creation.
 */
@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class User {
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
}
EOF
cat > src/test/java/com/example/model/UserTest.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.model;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class UserTest {

    @Test
    void lombokGeneratesAccessorsConstructorsAndBuilder() {
        User built = User.builder().id(1L).name("Ada").email("ada@example.com").build();
        User constructed = new User(1L, "Ada", "ada@example.com");

        User mutable = new User();
        mutable.setId(1L);
        mutable.setName("Ada");
        mutable.setEmail("ada@example.com");

        assertEquals("Ada", built.getName());
        assertEquals(built, constructed);
        assertEquals(built, mutable);
    }
}
EOF
cat > .gitignore <<'EOF'
target/
.idea/
*.iml
.vscode/
EOF
mvn -q -B verify 2>&1 | tail -30; echo EXIT=$?
